executor_result.summary: Add deterministic source-identity-based final tie-break to suppress_duplicates in normalization.py and fix cross-provider equal-rank test controls in test_contracts_normalization.py.

instructions: QUALITY AUDIT FIX ONLY, on exact base SHA. In part2/capital_flow/normalization.py, suppress_duplicates groups records by (family, metric, economic_event_id) and stable-sorts by (data_quality, attribution_quality, observed_at_ms) descending. Two PIT-visible cross-provider records of the SAME economic event with equal ranking fields but different source/source_record_id/value/provenance currently yield different winners when the input order is reversed, silently changing retained value/provenance and suppression decisions. Add a deterministic, documented, source-identity-based final tie-break (e.g. source, source_record_id, revision, observation_id) ONLY after existing quality, attribution, and observed_at_ms priorities; preserve existing higher-quality winner and no-dedup without economic_event_id. Add a deterministic regression in part2/capital_flow/tests/test_contracts_normalization.py using two different providers with the same family/metric/economic_event_id and identical primary ranking fields but distinct values and provenance; assert identical kept source/value/provenance and suppression decision identifiers under both input permutations. Include unequal-quality control, separate economic events, and missing economic_event_id guard. Preserve PIT availability filtering upstream, context-only isolation, dependence semantics, raw/audit provenance, and frozen scoring; do not invent evidence or change provider data, scoring formulas, or any other files. Executor must run targeted and full Capital Flow pytest and its built-in git diff --check, fail closed if tests fail. Never access private/main/Railway/prediction/API/journals/Telegram/MT5/broker/execution/secrets.
title: Deterministic cross-provider economic duplicate tie resolution
